topic: Execution and grouping of February 14 FGTB provincial actions
summary: The national FGTB page announces actions in five cities, but the opened post-event account verifies a large public gathering only in Marche-en-Famenne. Other cities’ actual gatherings, attendance and whether to group as one national event remain unresolved.
required_followup: Find permitted contemporaneous post-event coverage for the other sites; do not infer their attendance from the announcement.

topic: February 20 Iranian diaspora protest sources and Belgium policy scope
summary: The Brussels Times article is bylined “with Belga”; no independent body source has been opened. It reports a demand criticizing prisoner-transfer treaties signed by Belgium but the event’s principal demands target Iran and the EU. Reviewer should assess whether the explicit Belgian treaty-policy demand qualifies as an own-state target.
required_followup: Seek permitted independent reporting on the treaty demand and review own-state-target eligibility; do not infer a broader Belgium demand.

required_followup: No further research needed unless evidence identifies a distinct demand on Belgian policy.

topic: Valentine’s Day transport strikes and rallies
summary: The Brussels Times search-result article says transport unions planned a February 14 strike and rallies, while FGTB also announced provincial actions and a post-event FGTB branch report confirms a gathering in Marche-en-Famenne. Whether transport-union rallies were distinct from or part of the FGTB actions, whether other sites executed gatherings, and their sizes remain unresolved.
required_followup: Seek permitted post-event coverage to distinguish the transport-union action from the FGTB provincial gathering; do not duplicate or infer attendance.

topic: February 20 physical end and state response
summary: The article records the planned route and that the demonstration proceeded toward Cinquantenaire Park, but not its physical ending or response by Belgian authorities.
required_followup: Find a permitted source for the physical end and state response if material.

topic: Search method and historical source-access limits
summary: Open-web searches in English, French and Dutch used broad and weekly windows and local/regional sources, but are not equivalent to LexisNexis. Historical source ledgers are omitted and the new ledger is not a clean historical inventory. Known AP, HRW, NewArab, Facebook and L’Orient holds remain pending; none of their bodies were opened.
required_followup: Review any specifically needed missing source or archive when permitted; do not infer absence of protests from this search.
